Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 32, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat as-Sajdah [In manuscript A: "Surat Alif Lam Mim as-Sajdah."]

It is Meccan.

Al-Bukhari said in "The Book of Friday": Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A'raj, [In manuscript T: "And al-Bukhari narrated with his chain."] from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the Fajr prayer on Friday: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The revelation of the Book﴾, which is Surat as-Sajdah, and ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾.

Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (891), and Sahih Muslim, no. (880).]

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Salih informed us, from Layth, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would not sleep until he had recited ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The revelation of the Book﴾, which is Surat as-Sajdah, and ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾. Ahmad alone narrated it.

[Al-Musnad (3/340).]

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: there is no doubt or misgiving that it was sent down from the Lord of the worlds.

Then He said, reporting about the polytheists: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ Rather, they say: ﴿He has fabricated it﴾, i.e., he invented it of his own accord. ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, that they may be guided﴾, i.e., that they may follow the truth.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on verses 10–11 of Surah 32:

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about the polytheists in their denial of the Return (al-Ma'ad, the Resurrection), when they said: ﴿Could it be that when we have been lost in the earth,﴾ meaning: when our bodies have been torn apart and scattered into the parts of the earth [[In A: "the earths".]] and have gone away, ﴿Could it be that we will be in a new creation?﴾ meaning: Could it be that we will return after that state?! They deem this unlikely. This is only far-fetched relative to their own weak power, not relative to the power of the One who originated them and created them from nothing, whose command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it "Be," and it is. Therefore He said: ﴿Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you back.﴾ The apparent meaning of this verse is that the angel of death is a specific individual among the angels, as is evident from the hadith of al-Bara' mentioned earlier in Surah "Ibrahim" [[At verse 27; the hadith is given in full in manuscript T.]]. He has been named in some reports as 'Izra'il, and this is the well-known name, as stated by Qatadah and others. He has assistants. Likewise, it has been narrated in a hadith that his assistants pull the souls from all parts of the body, until, when they reach the throat, the angel of death receives them. [[In T: "as".]]

Mujahid said: The earth was gathered together for him and made like a basin (tast) for him, from which he takes whatever he wills. [[In T: "wishes".]] Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ) in similar form, as a mursal report. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) also said it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqri narrated to us, and [[In T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from"]] 'Amr ibn Shamir [[In T, F, A, H: "Umar ibn Sumrah," and the correction is from al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah and al-Mu'jam.]] from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the angel of death at the head of a man from the Ansar, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O angel of death, be gentle with my companion, for he is a believer." The angel of death said: "O Muhammad, be content and let your eye be cool, for I am gentle with every believer. Know that there is no house of clay or hair, on land or at sea, in the earth, except that I inspect it five times every day, so much so that I know their young and old better than they know themselves. By Allah, O Muhammad, if I wished to seize the soul of a gnat I would not be able to do so until Allah commands me to seize it." [[Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/220) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. (784), Kashf al-Astar, through the route of Isma'il ibn Aban, from 'Amr ibn Shamir al-Ju'fi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned something similar. He connected it and did not render it mursal. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isabah and said: "'Amr ibn Shamir is abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith)."]]

Ja'far said: It has reached me that he only inspects them at the times of the prayers. When he attends them at death, if the person is one who guards the prayer, the angel draws near to him, repels Satan from him, and the angel prompts him with: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," in that great state.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Mujahid say: There is no house of hair or clay on the face of the earth except that the angel of death circulates around it twice every day.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, there is no house in which any person of the worldly life dwells except that the angel of death stands at its door every day seven times, looking to see whether there is anyone in it whom he has been commanded to take. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

This is only far-fetched relative to their own weak power, not relative to the power of the One who originated them and created them from nothing, whose command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it "Be," and it is. Therefore He said: ﴿Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you back.﴾ The apparent meaning of this verse is that the angel of death is a specific individual among the angels, as is evident from the hadith of al-Bara' mentioned earlier in Surah "Ibrahim" [[At verse 27; the hadith is given in full in manuscript T.]]. He has been named in some reports as 'Izra'il, and this is the well-known name, as stated by Qatadah and others. He has assistants. Likewise, it has been narrated in a hadith that his assistants pull the souls from all parts of the body, until, when they reach the throat, the angel of death receives them. [[In T: "as".]]

Mujahid said: The earth was gathered together for him and made like a basin (tast) for him, from which he takes whatever he wills. [[In T: "wishes".]] Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ) in similar form, as a mursal report. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) also said it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqri narrated to us, and [[In T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from"]] 'Amr ibn Shamir [[In T, F, A, H: "Umar ibn Sumrah," and the correction is from al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah and al-Mu'jam.]] from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the angel of death at the head of a man from the Ansar, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O angel of death, be gentle with my companion, for he is a believer." The angel of death said: "O Muhammad, be content and let your eye be cool, for I am gentle with every believer. Know that there is no house of clay or hair, on land or at sea, in the earth, except that I inspect it five times every day, so much so that I know their young and old better than they know themselves. By Allah, O Muhammad, if I wished to seize the soul of a gnat I would not be able to do so until Allah commands me to seize it." [[Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/220) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. (784), Kashf al-Astar, through the route of Isma'il ibn Aban, from 'Amr ibn Shamir al-Ju'fi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned something similar. He connected it and did not render it mursal. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isabah and said: "'Amr ibn Shamir is abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith)."]]

Ja'far said: It has reached me that he only inspects them at the times of the prayers. When he attends them at death, if the person is one who guards the prayer, the angel draws near to him, repels Satan from him, and the angel prompts him with: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," in that great state.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Mujahid say: There is no house of hair or clay on the face of the earth except that the angel of death circulates around it twice every day.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, there is no house in which any person of the worldly life dwells except that the angel of death stands at its door every day seven times, looking to see whether there is anyone in it whom he has been commanded to take. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned,﴾ meaning: on the Day of your Return (ma'ad), and your rising from your graves for your recompense.

The Most High informs us about the state of the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, and about their condition when they witness the Resurrection. They stand before Allah humiliated and abased, with their heads bowed, that is, out of shame and embarrassment, and they say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾ [[Following this in manuscripts F and A: "So return us, that we may do righteousness."]] That is: we now hear Your speech and obey Your command, as the Most High said: ﴿How well they will hear and see on the day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38]. Likewise, when they enter the Fire, they reproach themselves, saying: ﴿If we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. Thus these people say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us﴾, that is, to the worldly abode, ﴿that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain﴾, that is, they have now become certain and verified that Your promise is true and that meeting You is true. The Lord, the Most High, knew about them that if He returned them to the worldly abode, they would be exactly as they were there, disbelievers who deny the signs of Allah and oppose His messengers, as He said: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." Rather, there has become apparent to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. And they said, "There is nothing but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected"﴾ [al-An'am: 27–29].

Here He said: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, as the Most High said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [Yunus: 99].

﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ That is, from both categories. So their abode is the Fire, from which they have no escape and no means of deliverance. We seek refuge in Allah and His perfect words from that.

﴿So taste, for having forgotten the meeting of this your Day﴾. That is, it is said to the people of the Fire, by way of rebuke and reproach: taste the punishment [this] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] because of your denial of it, your deeming its occurrence far-fetched, and your forgetting of it, since you treated it as one treats something that is forgotten. ﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾, that is, [indeed] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] We will treat you as one treats the forgotten, because He, the Most High, forgets nothing and nothing escapes His knowledge. Rather, this is by way of reciprocity, as the Most High said: ﴿Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34].

* *

His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity because of what you used to do﴾, that is, because of your disbelief and denial, as He said in another verse: ﴿They will not taste therein coolness or drink, except boiling water and dark, foul liquid, as a fitting recompense. Indeed, they used not to expect an account, and they denied Our signs with complete denial. And all things We have enumerated in a Record. So taste; We will not increase you except in punishment﴾ [al-Naba': 24–30].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration﴾, that is, they only affirm them. ﴿Those who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate﴾, meaning: they listen to them and obey them in word and deed. ﴿And they glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾ [meaning] towards following them and submitting to them, unlike what the ignorant disbelievers and sinners do. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled﴾ [Ghafir 40:60].

Then He said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, meaning by this: the night prayer, and abandoning sleep and lying down on soft bedding. Mujahid and al-Hasan said concerning His words: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, meaning by this: the night prayer.

And it is narrated from Anas, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, Abu Hazim and Qatadah that it is the prayer between the two evening prayers (al-Maghrib and al-Isha'). And it is also narrated from Anas: it is waiting for the 'Atamah prayer (al-Isha'). Ibn Jarir narrated it with a good chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/63)]

Al-Dahhak said: it is the 'Isha' prayer in congregation and the Fajr prayer in congregation.

﴿They call upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾, that is, fearing the severity of His punishment and hoping for His abundant reward. ﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾. Thus they combine obligatory and voluntary acts of worship, both those that are restricted to the self and those that benefit others. The foremost of these, their leader, their master and their pride in this world and the Hereafter, is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

"And among us is the Messenger of Allah, who recites His Book,
When the light of dawn breaks forth, shining.
He showed us guidance after blindness, so our hearts
Are certain, by him, that what he said will come to pass.
He spends the night, drawing his side away from his bed,
When the bedding of the polytheists becomes heavy with them."

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh and ʿAffan narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Your Lord marvels at two men: a man who rises from his quilt and his blanket, from between his family and his beloved, to his prayer; so your Lord says: O My angels, look at My servant, who has risen from his bed and his bedding, from between his beloved and his family, to his prayer, out of desire for what is with Me and compassion for what is with Me. And a man who fought in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they fled; he knew what was upon him of fleeing and what was for him in returning, so he returned until his blood was spilled, out of desire for what is with Me and compassion for what is with Me. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the angels: Look at My servant who returned out of desire for what is with Me and fear of what is with Me, until his blood was spilled."

Abu Dawud narrated it likewise in "al-Jihad", from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with similar wording. [Musnad (1/416) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5236)]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Wa'il, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and one morning I was near him as we were travelling, so I said: O Prophet of Allah, inform me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: "You have asked about something great, and it is indeed easy for one for whom Allah makes it easy: worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, pay the zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House." Then he said: "Shall I not direct you to the gates of good? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man's prayer in the depths of the night." Then he recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, until he reached ﴿they used to do﴾. Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and the peak of its hump?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and the peak of its hump is jihad in the way of Allah." Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the key to all of that?" I said: Yes, O Prophet of Allah. He took hold of his tongue and said: "Restrain this upon yourself." I said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be held accountable for what we say? He said: "May your mother be bereaved of you, O Mu'adh! Will people be thrown into the Fire on their faces, or on their noses, except for the harvest of their tongues?"

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it in their Sunans, through several routes from Ma'mar, with the same chain. [Musnad (5/231), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2616), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11394), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3973)] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard ʿUrwah ibn al-Nazzal narrate from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Shall I not direct you to the gates of good: fasting is a shield, charity atones for sin, and the standing of a servant in the depths of the night," and he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/64)]

He also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording; and from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit and al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, marfu' with similar wording. And from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Shahr, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, he said: "The servant's standing in the night." [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/64, 65)]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Fitr ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Hakam and Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the battle of Tabuk, and he said: "If you wish, I will inform you of the gates of good: fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man's standing in the depths of the night," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾.

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, ʿAli ibn Musهir narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who narrated from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out with a voice that the creatures hear: 'Let the people of the gathering know today who is most deserving of honour.' Then he will return and call: 'Let those whose sides forsook their beds arise,' and they will rise, and they will be few." [Also narrated by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in his Musnad, and Abu Ya'la in al-Musnad al-Kabir, as in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (4/373), from the hadith of Asma' bint Yazid, may Allah be pleased with her.]

Al-Bazzar said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib narrated to us, al-Walid ibn ʿAta' ibn al-Aghurr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mus'ab informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: Bilal said, when this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, [the verse]: "We used to sit in the gathering, and some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray between Maghrib and 'Isha', then this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾."

Then he said: We do not know that Aslam narrated from Bilal other than this, and this is the only route from Bilal. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2250), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/90): "In it is ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib, who is weak."]

* *

His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾, that is: no one knows the greatness of what Allah has hidden for them in the Gardens of lasting bliss, and the pleasures the like of which no one has ever witnessed. Since they concealed their deeds, Allah concealed for them of the reward, as a fitting recompense; for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: A people concealed their deeds, so Allah concealed for them what no eye has seen, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human being. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Bukhari said: concerning His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾, the verse: Ali ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Abu Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾.

He said: Sufyan also narrated to us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Allah said the like of it. It was asked of Sufyan: As a narration? He said: Then what else?

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4779), Sahih Muslim no. (2824), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3197)] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Then al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, narrated to us Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, a store apart from what you have been shown," then he recited: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

Abu Mu'awiyah said, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih: Abu Hurayrah recited "qurrat a'yun" (delights of eyes). Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4780), and in al-Bukhari the "narration of Abu Mu'awiyah" after the preceding hadith.]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs through the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzaq. [Musnad (2/313); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (8498) through ʿAbd Allah from Ma'mar; I did not find it in the Sahihs through ʿAbd al-Razzaq's narration.] It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the like of it. Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3292), Tafsir al-Tabari (21/66)]

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, Hammad said: I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever enters Paradise will be in bliss and will not despair; his garments will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. In Paradise is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim no. (2836)]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 32, verses 15–17 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad narrated: Harun narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, that Abu Hazim narrated to him, saying: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "I witnessed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a gathering in which he described Paradise, until he finished. Then at the end of his hadith he said: 'In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.'" Then he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾, up to His saying: ﴿they used to do﴾.

Muslim also recorded it in his Sahih from Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Harun ibn Sa'id, both from Ibn Wahb, with the same chain. [Musnad (5/334) and Sahih Muslim no. (2825).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, Sallam ibn Abi Muti' narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Uqbah ibn Abd al-Ghafir, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who related from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." They (the compilers of the six books) did not record it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/67).]

Muslim also said in his Sahih: Ibn Abi Umar and others narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Mutarrif ibn Tarif and Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both having heard al-Sha'bi report from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: "I heard him (al-Sha'bi) on the pulpit, raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: 'Musa, peace be upon him, asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: What is the lowest rank among the people of Paradise? He said: He is a man who comes after the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, and it will be said to him: Enter Paradise. He will say: My Lord, how (can I), when the people have taken their places and taken their shares? It will be said to him: Would you be pleased that you have the like of the kingdom of a king among the kings of the world? He will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He will be told: For you is that, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it. In the fifth he will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He will be told: This is for you, and ten times its like, and for you is whatever your soul desires and your eye delights in. He will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He (Musa) said: My Lord, then what of the highest in rank? He said: Those are the ones whom I intended; I planted their honor with My own hand and sealed it, so no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to any human heart.'" He (al-Mughirah) said: "And its confirmation from the Book of Allah is: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Abi Umar and said: "Hasan sahih." He said: "Some of them narrated it from al-Sha'bi, from al-Mughirah, without raising it (to the Prophet), but the raised version is more sound." [Sahih Muslim no. (189) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3198).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Munir al-Mada'ini narrated to us, Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Khaythamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Juhadah, from Amir ibn Abd al-Wahid, who said: "It reached me that a man from the people of Paradise will remain in his place for seventy years, then he will turn and find a woman more beautiful than what he was in. She will say to him: Has the time come for us to have a share of you? He will say: Who are you? She will say: I am from the Additional (al-Mazid). He will remain with her for seventy years. Then he will turn and find a woman more beautiful than what he was in, and she will say to him: Has the time come for us to have a share of you? He will say: Who are you? She will say: I am the one of whom Allah said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾."

Ibn Lahi'ah said: Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The angels will enter upon them at the measure of each day of the days of the world, three times, bringing gifts from Allah from the Gardens of Eden, which are not in their gardens. This is His saying: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, and they will be told that Allah is pleased with them."

Ibn Jarir said: Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Abu al-Yaman al-Hawzani, or another, who said: "Paradise has one hundred levels. The first level is silver: its ground is silver, its dwellings are silver, its vessels are silver, and its dust is musk. The second is gold: its ground is gold, its dwellings are gold, its vessels are gold, and its dust is musk. The third is pearl: its ground is pearl, its dwellings are pearl, its vessels are pearl, and its dust is musk. And ninety-seven after that, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Then he recited this verse: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/66).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from al-Ghitrif, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin, i.e., Jibril), who said: "The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant are brought, and some of them are subtracted from others. If one good deed remains, Allah will widen for him in Paradise." He said: "I entered upon Yazdad, and he narrated a similar hadith." He said: "I said: Then where did the good deed go?" He said: He recited: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their bad deeds, among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. I said: As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, he said: "It is the servant who does something secretly between himself and Allah, which the people do not know about, so Allah will hide for him on the Day of Resurrection a comfort for the eyes." [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/67).]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration﴾, that is, they only affirm them. ﴿Those who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate﴾, meaning: they listen to them and obey them in word and deed. ﴿And they glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾ [meaning] towards following them and submitting to them, unlike what the ignorant disbelievers and sinners do. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled﴾ [Ghafir 40:60].

Then He said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, meaning by this: the night prayer, and abandoning sleep and lying down on soft bedding. Mujahid and al-Hasan said concerning His words: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, meaning by this: the night prayer.

And it is narrated from Anas, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, Abu Hazim and Qatadah that it is the prayer between the two evening prayers (al-Maghrib and al-Isha'). And it is also narrated from Anas: it is waiting for the 'Atamah prayer (al-Isha'). Ibn Jarir narrated it with a good chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/63)]

Al-Dahhak said: it is the 'Isha' prayer in congregation and the Fajr prayer in congregation.

﴿They call upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾, that is, fearing the severity of His punishment and hoping for His abundant reward. ﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾. Thus they combine obligatory and voluntary acts of worship, both those that are restricted to the self and those that benefit others. The foremost of these, their leader, their master and their pride in this world and the Hereafter, is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

"And among us is the Messenger of Allah, who recites His Book,
When the light of dawn breaks forth, shining.
He showed us guidance after blindness, so our hearts
Are certain, by him, that what he said will come to pass.
He spends the night, drawing his side away from his bed,
When the bedding of the polytheists becomes heavy with them."

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh and ʿAffan narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Your Lord marvels at two men: a man who rises from his quilt and his blanket, from between his family and his beloved, to his prayer; so your Lord says: O My angels, look at My servant, who has risen from his bed and his bedding, from between his beloved and his family, to his prayer, out of desire for what is with Me and compassion for what is with Me. And a man who fought in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they fled; he knew what was upon him of fleeing and what was for him in returning, so he returned until his blood was spilled, out of desire for what is with Me and compassion for what is with Me. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the angels: Look at My servant who returned out of desire for what is with Me and fear of what is with Me, until his blood was spilled."

Abu Dawud narrated it likewise in "al-Jihad", from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with similar wording. [Musnad (1/416) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5236)]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Wa'il, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and one morning I was near him as we were travelling, so I said: O Prophet of Allah, inform me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: "You have asked about something great, and it is indeed easy for one for whom Allah makes it easy: worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, pay the zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House." Then he said: "Shall I not direct you to the gates of good? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man's prayer in the depths of the night." Then he recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, until he reached ﴿they used to do﴾. Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and the peak of its hump?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and the peak of its hump is jihad in the way of Allah." Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the key to all of that?" I said: Yes, O Prophet of Allah. He took hold of his tongue and said: "Restrain this upon yourself." I said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be held accountable for what we say? He said: "May your mother be bereaved of you, O Mu'adh! Will people be thrown into the Fire on their faces, or on their noses, except for the harvest of their tongues?"

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it in their Sunans, through several routes from Ma'mar, with the same chain. [Musnad (5/231), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2616), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11394), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3973)] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard ʿUrwah ibn al-Nazzal narrate from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Shall I not direct you to the gates of good: fasting is a shield, charity atones for sin, and the standing of a servant in the depths of the night," and he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/64)]

He also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording; and from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit and al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, marfu' with similar wording. And from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Shahr, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, he said: "The servant's standing in the night." [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/64, 65)]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Fitr ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Hakam and Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the battle of Tabuk, and he said: "If you wish, I will inform you of the gates of good: fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man's standing in the depths of the night," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾.

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, ʿAli ibn Musهir narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who narrated from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out with a voice that the creatures hear: 'Let the people of the gathering know today who is most deserving of honour.' Then he will return and call: 'Let those whose sides forsook their beds arise,' and they will rise, and they will be few." [Also narrated by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in his Musnad, and Abu Ya'la in al-Musnad al-Kabir, as in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (4/373), from the hadith of Asma' bint Yazid, may Allah be pleased with her.]

Al-Bazzar said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib narrated to us, al-Walid ibn ʿAta' ibn al-Aghurr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mus'ab informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: Bilal said, when this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, [the verse]: "We used to sit in the gathering, and some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray between Maghrib and 'Isha', then this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾."

Then he said: We do not know that Aslam narrated from Bilal other than this, and this is the only route from Bilal. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2250), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/90): "In it is ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib, who is weak."]

* *

His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾, that is: no one knows the greatness of what Allah has hidden for them in the Gardens of lasting bliss, and the pleasures the like of which no one has ever witnessed. Since they concealed their deeds, Allah concealed for them of the reward, as a fitting recompense; for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: A people concealed their deeds, so Allah concealed for them what no eye has seen, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human being. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Bukhari said: concerning His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾, the verse: Ali ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Abu Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾.

He said: Sufyan also narrated to us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Allah said the like of it. It was asked of Sufyan: As a narration? He said: Then what else?

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4779), Sahih Muslim no. (2824), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3197)] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Then al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, narrated to us Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, a store apart from what you have been shown," then he recited: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

Abu Mu'awiyah said, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih: Abu Hurayrah recited "qurrat a'yun" (delights of eyes). Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4780), and in al-Bukhari the "narration of Abu Mu'awiyah" after the preceding hadith.]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs through the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzaq. [Musnad (2/313); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (8498) through ʿAbd Allah from Ma'mar; I did not find it in the Sahihs through ʿAbd al-Razzaq's narration.] It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the like of it. Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3292), Tafsir al-Tabari (21/66)]

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, Hammad said: I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever enters Paradise will be in bliss and will not despair; his garments will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. In Paradise is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim no. (2836)]

Then at the end of his hadith he said: 'In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.'" When the bedding of the polytheists becomes heavy with them."

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh and ʿAffan narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Your Lord marvels at two men: a man who rises from his quilt and his blanket, from between his family and his beloved, to his prayer; so your Lord says: O My angels, look at My servant, who has risen from his bed and his bedding, from between his beloved and his family, to his prayer, out of desire for what is with Me and compassion for what is with Me. And a man who fought in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they fled; he knew what was upon him of fleeing and what was for him in returning, so he returned until his blood was spilled, out of desire for what is with Me and compassion for what is with Me. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the angels: Look at My servant who returned out of desire for what is with Me and fear of what is with Me, until his blood was spilled."

Abu Dawud narrated it likewise in "al-Jihad", from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with similar wording. [Musnad (1/416) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5236)]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Wa'il, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and one morning I was near him as we were travelling, so I said: O Prophet of Allah, inform me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: "You have asked about something great, and it is indeed easy for one for whom Allah makes it easy: worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, pay the zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House." Then he said: "Shall I not direct you to the gates of good? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man's prayer in the depths of the night." Then he recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, until he reached ﴿they used to do﴾. Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and the peak of its hump?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and the peak of its hump is jihad in the way of Allah." Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the key to all of that?" I said: Yes, O Prophet of Allah. He took hold of his tongue and said: "Restrain this upon yourself." I said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be held accountable for what we say? He said: "May your mother be bereaved of you, O Mu'adh! Will people be thrown into the Fire on their faces, or on their noses, except for the harvest of their tongues?"

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it in their Sunans, through several routes from Ma'mar, with the same chain. [Musnad (5/231), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2616), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11394), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3973)] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard ʿUrwah ibn al-Nazzal narrate from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Shall I not direct you to the gates of good: fasting is a shield, charity atones for sin, and the standing of a servant in the depths of the night," and he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/64)]

He also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording; and from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit and al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, marfu' with similar wording. And from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Shahr, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, he said: "The servant's standing in the night." [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/64, 65)]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Fitr ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Hakam and Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the battle of Tabuk, and he said: "If you wish, I will inform you of the gates of good: fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man's standing in the depths of the night," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾.

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, ʿAli ibn Musهir narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who narrated from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out with a voice that the creatures hear: 'Let the people of the gathering know today who is most deserving of honour.' Then he will return and call: 'Let those whose sides forsook their beds arise,' and they will rise, and they will be few." [Also narrated by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in his Musnad, and Abu Ya'la in al-Musnad al-Kabir, as in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (4/373), from the hadith of Asma' bint Yazid, may Allah be pleased with her.]

Al-Bazzar said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib narrated to us, al-Walid ibn ʿAta' ibn al-Aghurr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mus'ab informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: Bilal said, when this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, [the verse]: "We used to sit in the gathering, and some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray between Maghrib and 'Isha', then this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾."

Then he said: We do not know that Aslam narrated from Bilal other than this, and this is the only route from Bilal. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2250), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/90): "In it is ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib, who is weak."]

* *

His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾, that is: no one knows the greatness of what Allah has hidden for them in the Gardens of lasting bliss, and the pleasures the like of which no one has ever witnessed. Since they concealed their deeds, Allah concealed for them of the reward, as a fitting recompense; for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: A people concealed their deeds, so Allah concealed for them what no eye has seen, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human being. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Bukhari said: concerning His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾, the verse: Ali ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Abu Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾.

He said: Sufyan also narrated to us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Allah said the like of it. It was asked of Sufyan: As a narration? He said: Then what else?

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4779), Sahih Muslim no. (2824), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3197)] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Then al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, narrated to us Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, a store apart from what you have been shown," then he recited: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

Abu Mu'awiyah said, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih: Abu Hurayrah recited "qurrat a'yun" (delights of eyes). Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4780), and in al-Bukhari the "narration of Abu Mu'awiyah" after the preceding hadith.]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs through the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzaq. [Musnad (2/313); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (8498) through ʿAbd Allah from Ma'mar; I did not find it in the Sahihs through ʿAbd al-Razzaq's narration.] It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the like of it. Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3292), Tafsir al-Tabari (21/66)]

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, Hammad said: I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever enters Paradise will be in bliss and will not despair; his garments will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. In Paradise is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim no. (2836)]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 32, verses 15–17 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad narrated: Harun narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, that Abu Hazim narrated to him, saying: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "I witnessed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a gathering in which he described Paradise, until he finished. Then at the end of his hadith he said: 'In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.'" Then he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾, up to His saying: ﴿they used to do﴾.

Muslim also recorded it in his Sahih from Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Harun ibn Sa'id, both from Ibn Wahb, with the same chain. [Musnad (5/334) and Sahih Muslim no. (2825).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, Sallam ibn Abi Muti' narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Uqbah ibn Abd al-Ghafir, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who related from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." They (the compilers of the six books) did not record it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/67).]

Muslim also said in his Sahih: Ibn Abi Umar and others narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Mutarrif ibn Tarif and Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both having heard al-Sha'bi report from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: "I heard him (al-Sha'bi) on the pulpit, raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: 'Musa, peace be upon him, asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: What is the lowest rank among the people of Paradise? He said: He is a man who comes after the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, and it will be said to him: Enter Paradise. He will say: My Lord, how (can I), when the people have taken their places and taken their shares? It will be said to him: Would you be pleased that you have the like of the kingdom of a king among the kings of the world? He will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He will be told: For you is that, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it. In the fifth he will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He will be told: This is for you, and ten times its like, and for you is whatever your soul desires and your eye delights in. He will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He (Musa) said: My Lord, then what of the highest in rank? He said: Those are the ones whom I intended; I planted their honor with My own hand and sealed it, so no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to any human heart.'" He (al-Mughirah) said: "And its confirmation from the Book of Allah is: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Abi Umar and said: "Hasan sahih." He said: "Some of them narrated it from al-Sha'bi, from al-Mughirah, without raising it (to the Prophet), but the raised version is more sound." [Sahih Muslim no. (189) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3198).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Munir al-Mada'ini narrated to us, Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Khaythamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Juhadah, from Amir ibn Abd al-Wahid, who said: "It reached me that a man from the people of Paradise will remain in his place for seventy years, then he will turn and find a woman more beautiful than what he was in. She will say to him: Has the time come for us to have a share of you? He will say: Who are you? She will say: I am from the Additional (al-Mazid). He will remain with her for seventy years. Then he will turn and find a woman more beautiful than what he was in, and she will say to him: Has the time come for us to have a share of you? He will say: Who are you? She will say: I am the one of whom Allah said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾."

Ibn Lahi'ah said: Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The angels will enter upon them at the measure of each day of the days of the world, three times, bringing gifts from Allah from the Gardens of Eden, which are not in their gardens. This is His saying: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, and they will be told that Allah is pleased with them."

Ibn Jarir said: Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Abu al-Yaman al-Hawzani, or another, who said: "Paradise has one hundred levels. The first level is silver: its ground is silver, its dwellings are silver, its vessels are silver, and its dust is musk. The second is gold: its ground is gold, its dwellings are gold, its vessels are gold, and its dust is musk. The third is pearl: its ground is pearl, its dwellings are pearl, its vessels are pearl, and its dust is musk. And ninety-seven after that, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Then he recited this verse: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/66).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from al-Ghitrif, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin, i.e., Jibril), who said: "The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant are brought, and some of them are subtracted from others. If one good deed remains, Allah will widen for him in Paradise." He said: "I entered upon Yazdad, and he narrated a similar hadith." He said: "I said: Then where did the good deed go?" He said: He recited: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their bad deeds, among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. I said: As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, he said: "It is the servant who does something secretly between himself and Allah, which the people do not know about, so Allah will hide for him on the Day of Resurrection a comfort for the eyes." [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/67).]

God, the Exalted, informs us of His justice [and His generosity] [[addition from manuscript A.]] that on the Day of Resurrection He does not treat as equal, in His judgment, the one who believes in His signs and follows His messengers and the one who is defiant (fasiq), that is, one who has departed from obedience to his Lord and denied His messengers sent to him [[in manuscripts T and F: "the messengers of God"]], as He said: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, that their living and their dying will be equal? Evil is what they judge.﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 21] And He said: ﴿Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters on earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28] And He said: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the ones who will be triumphant.﴾ [Al-Hashr: 20] Therefore He said here: ﴿Is the one who is a believer like the one who is defiant? They are not equal﴾, meaning: in the sight of God on the Day of Resurrection.

It has been reported by ʿAtaʾ ibn Yasar, al-Suddi and others that this verse was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. Therefore He made their judgment explicit, saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: their hearts affirmed the signs of God and they acted in accordance with what they required [[in T: "their hearts believed in the meeting with God and in its requirements"]], and these are the righteous deeds. ﴿For them are the Gardens of Refuge (Jannat al-Maʾwa)﴾, meaning: gardens in which there are dwellings, mansions and lofty chambers. ﴿As a welcome (nuzul)﴾, meaning: as hospitality and honor, ﴿for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿As for those who were defiant﴾, meaning: those who departed from obedience, ﴿their refuge is the Fire. Whenever they wish to get out of it, they will be returned to it﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whenever they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned to it﴾ [Al-Hajj: 22].

Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad said: "By God, indeed the hands are bound, the feet are shackled, the flame lifts them up, and the angels strike them down."

﴿And it will be said to them: "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ meaning: this is said to them as rebuke and reproach.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment (al-ʿadhab al-adna) short of the greater punishment, so that they may return﴾ [[addition from T.]] Ibn ʿAbbas said: By "the lesser punishment" is meant the calamities of this world, its sicknesses and afflictions, and what befalls its people, with which God tests His servants so that they may turn back to Him in repentance. The same has been reported from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Dahhak, ʿAlqamah, ʿAtiyyah, Mujahid, Qatadah, ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari, and Khasif.

Ibn ʿAbbas also said, in another narration from him: It means the enforcement of the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them.

Al-Bara ibn ʿAzib, Mujahid, and Abu ʿUbaydah said: It means the punishment of the grave.

Al-Nasai said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Israʾil, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas and Abu ʿUbaydah [[in T: "Al-Nasai narrated with his chain"]], from ʿAbd Allah (ibn Masʿud), regarding ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment﴾, he said: "Years of drought that afflicted them." [[Al-Nasai in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11395.]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: My father narrated to me, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from ʿAzrah [[in F and A: "ʿUrwah"]], from al-Hasan al-ʿUranī, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Ibn Abi Layla [[in T: "ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad narrated"]], from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb regarding this verse: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment﴾, he said: "The calamities and the smoke have already passed, and the (great) seizing and the constant punishment (al-lizam)." [[Zawaʾid al-Musnad 5/128.]]

Muslim narrated it through the narration of Shuʿbah, with the same meaning, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not traced to the Prophet). [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2799.]] And in al-Bukhari, from Ibn Masʿud, something similar, with the wording: "Five have passed: the smoke, the Byzantines, the moon, the seizing, and the constant punishment." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4820.]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud also said, in another narration from him: The lesser punishment is what befell them of killing and captivity on the day of Badr. Malik also said the same, from Zayd ibn Aslam.

Al-Suddi and others said: No house in Mecca remained without entering into it grief over a slain or captured man of theirs, so they were afflicted, or defeated; and among them were those in whom both afflictions were combined.

As for His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turns away from them?﴾, meaning: none is more unjust than the one whom God reminded of His signs, and made them clear to him and explained them, and then after that he abandoned them, denied them, turned away from them and forgot them, as if he did not know them.

Qatadah, may God have mercy on him, said: Beware of turning away from the remembrance of God, for whoever turns away from His remembrance has been deceived by the greatest deception, has become exposed to the worst of harm, and has magnified among the greatest sins.

For this reason God, the Exalted, said, threatening those who do that: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾, meaning: I will surely take the most severe retribution against those who do that.

Ibn Jarir said: ʿImran ibn Bakkar al-Kilaʿi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from ʿUbadah ibn Nusayy, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah [[in T: "Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain"]], from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Whoever does three things has committed a crime: whoever raises a banner for an unjust cause, or disobeys his parents, or walks with an oppressor to support him, has committed a crime." God says: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari 21/69.]] Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it through the narration of Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash, with the same chain, and this is a very strange (gharib) hadith.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 32, verses 23–25:

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about His servant and messenger Musa (peace be upon him), that He gave him the Book, which is the Torah.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾: Qatadah said, "It refers to the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey)." [[In manuscript T: "al-Asra" (the Night Journey).]] Then it is narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, who said: "Ibn 'Amm Nabiyyikum (the paternal cousin of your Prophet), meaning Ibn 'Abbas, told me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I was shown Musa ibn 'Imran, a man of brown complexion, tall, with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah. I saw 'Isa, a man of medium build, inclining to red and white, with straight hair. I saw Malik, the keeper of the Fire, and the Dajjal, among the signs which Allah showed me.'" So ﴿do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾ means that you have seen Musa and met him on the night you were taken on the Night Journey. [[See the narration at the commentary on the first verse of Surah al-Isra' and its takhrij (sourcing) there.]]

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to us; Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us; Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, that he said: "Musa was made a guidance for the Children of Israel." And concerning His saying ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾, he said: "It means the meeting of Musa with his Lord, mighty and majestic." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (12/160). Had the intended meaning been the conquest of Makkah, their Islam would not have been accepted, given His words: ﴿Say: "On the Day of Victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."﴾ Rather, the intended "victory" is the *fath* in the sense of judgment and decision, as in His words: ﴿Judge between me and them with a judgment, and save me and those with me of the believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 118]; and His words: ﴿Say: "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us with truth, and He is the Judge, the All-Knowing."﴾ [Saba': 26]; and His words: ﴿They sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed﴾ [Ibrahim: 15]; and He said: ﴿And they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89]; and He said: ﴿If you seek a judgment, the judgment has certainly come to you﴾ [al-Anfal: 19].

And wait, for Allah will surely fulfill for you what He has promised you, and He will give you victory over whoever opposes you. Indeed, He does not fail in His promise.
